reason: The hypothesis proposes microalloying a refractory high-entropy alloy with Y2O3 nanoparticles, an oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) approach. While ODS is a well-known concept (mentioned in P37 for steels), none of the provided passages study or propose Y2O3 nanoparticle addition to any RHEA for combined mechanical enhancement and thermal/irradiation stability. The passages focus on compositional tuning (e.g., adding Hf, Cr, Co, Ni, C, B) or grain size effects, not on introducing a ceramic dispersoid phase. The mechanism (Orowan looping, grain boundary pinning) is textbook knowledge, but its application to a RHEA in this specific context is not suggested by any passage.

increase in yield strength and hardness
grain size stability and irradiation resistance as baseline properties
